messages:
Sam: quick thread — proposing a simplification of tiers + quota semantics. goal: fewer surprise 429s, clearer overage paths, and a migration that won’t require contractual renegotiation for most customers. thoughts?
Liam: curious — what do you mean by 'simplification'? aggregate tokens per-minute or per-second burst buckets?
Sam: primary idea = two-layer model: steady-rate (tokens/min) + burst credits (short lived, tokens/sec). steady-rate maps to a tier. burst credits are purchased or allocated on commit. default overage = soft-throttle with queued retries for non-critical calls.
Maya: need pricing model immediately. do we plan per-token overage, flat monthly burst add-ons, or both? revenue modeling depends a lot.
Rao: customers have asked for predictable burst on launches. they'd rather pay for a burst pool than face a hard 429 during product launches. enterprise sales will push for contractual burst pools.
Olivia: from CS: migration messaging is key. many teams don’t monitor X-RateLimit headers today. we should offer an SDK patch + a migration guide and an opt-in migration window. otherwise support spike incoming.
Jules: legal flag: any overage auto-charges require opt-in in some regions. EU contracts may need explicit consent for auto-billing. also watch refund rules.
deploy-bot: Sam requested a rollout checklist: tickets created: #PRICING-487, #SDK-221, #BILL-98
Liam: implementation notes: runtime needs token-bucket per-customer + global burst pool accounting. KV cache hit rate affects tokens consumed vs billed — we need to define whether cached responses consume quota.
Sam: good point — proposal: cached prefix hits count as 10% of tokens to avoid abuse but still incentivize caching. open to pushback.
Maya: 10% feels arbitrary. we should model three scenarios (0%, 10%, 100%) for ARR impact over 6 months and include churn risk.
Rao: commercial ask: offer a "launch day" one-time burst credit (e.g., 1M tokens) for new customers or paid as add-on. Sales needs an SKU and a simple add-on flow in the console.
Olivia: CS can own a migration concierge for top 20 customers. for self-serve, include an automated migration tool + compatibility mode for 30 days.
Sam: Launch criteria (draft):
- Docs: migration guide + API header spec
- SDKs: auto-retry + headers surfaced
- Billing: console SKU + billing UI + opt-in overage consent for EU
- Infra: per-customer token buckets + burst accounting + metrics
- Pilot: 5 pilot customers onboarded and no more than 3 critical support tickets in pilot week
- Metrics: <0.5% increase in 429s after migration, adoption of burst SKU by at least 15% of pilots
Liam: need to add performance SLOs: any new checks should add <5ms p50 and <15ms p99 to request processing.
Maya: finance asks for a break-even analysis and suggested list price for burst SKUs. I'll run numbers on 3 scenarios and share by EOD Thu.
Jules: add compliance checklist: auto-bill consent logs retained, opt-out flows, and audit trail for manual credits.
Sam: rollout plan idea: feature-flagged in hosted -> Dedicated as opt-in -> Private (customer-managed) templates + docs. GA after 6 weeks of pilot validation.
Rao: for sales enablement: need one-pager, pricing matrix, migration FAQ, and contract language snippets. I'll coordinate with legal.
Olivia: I'll prepare CS playbook + email templates for migration communication.
Liam: technical open questions:
```
# pseudo-config
quota: {
  steady_rate: 60000 # tokens per minute
  burst_pool: 1000000 # tokens (shared), reset window: 24h
  cache_charge_percent: 10
}
```
Will this require a schema change to usages API? yes. we need a migration path for historical billing data.
Sam: yes, usages API will include new fields in the header and payload. we’ll version the API (v2/usages) and keep v1 live for 3 months.
Maya: finance: keep v1 for 3 months only if we can backfill invoices accurately. otherwise extend.
Jules: recommend adding explicit consent checkbox in console for auto-overages for EU customers.
Sam: decision points we need to resolve by EOW:
- cached requests billing % (0/10/100)
- burst SKU price bands and default pilot credit size
- opt-in vs opt-out for auto-overages in key regions
- SDK surface for retry/backoff (we prefer server-side queueing + client retriable 429)
Liam: engineering estimate: 6w to build runtime hooks + 2w SDK + 2w billing + 1w rollout tooling = ~11w, includes QA. can parallelize SDK + billing.
Maya: finance + product sync Thu 10am to review modeling. sending calendar invite.
Rao: @here can we commit to the pilot roster? I'll propose 6 potential customers that asked for burst guarantees.
Olivia: noted. CS will follow up with onboarding playbook drafts by next Tue.
Sam: thanks all. I'll update the doc with the final scope after Thu meeting. please react on parts you own. :thumbsup:
Jules: :thumbsup:
